text:
**For most buyers, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** Every source here agrees on that, with a few caveats.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** Typical ratings are about 3,000-4,000 cycles to 80% for LFP versus 500-800 for the NMC units in the spec tables. Daily use would wear out a 500-cycle NMC unit in under two years, versus roughly 8-11 years for LFP ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). One source claims 1,000-2,000 for NMC, so ratings vary.
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests on small cells, LFP failures were milder. One test peaked at 259°C for LFP versus 731°C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). However, LFP isn't fireproof, and in one overcharge test it hit thermal runaway sooner ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). It's still a real advantage for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Price:** The median price per Wh is about $0.55 for LFP versus $0.95 for NMC in one catalog ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Cost per rated cycle is much lower for LFP.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Energy density:** NMC cells hold more energy per pound. In finished power stations the gap shrinks a lot, because the inverter and case weigh the same either way. One database found only about 10% difference at the median, and some LFP units are lighter per Wh than NMC ones ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).

**Cold weather:** Chemistry matters less than you'd think. Most LFP and NMC stations alike won't charge below 32°F, so check the specific manual ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**When NMC is fine**
- You'd use it only a few times a year, such as for rare outages, since time will age the battery before cycles do.
- Weight is critical.
- You already own a working NMC unit.

**Shopping tips**
- Check the spec sheet for "LiFePO4" or "LFP." Some makers don't state the chemistry.
- Compare the cycle rating's end point (70% vs. 80%), since a rating to 70% promises less.
- Pick on fit first (output watts and capacity), chemistry second.
